## Goal

# Goal — Creativity: Evolutionary Search for Useful Possibilities

Status: **operator-directed draft, non-canonical implementation input**.
This goal records the intended outcome and boundaries for Brainstorming. It
does not launch a session or authorize implementation, and it does not allocate
milestones, slices, or delivery stages.

## Outcome

Add a first-class task, provisionally named **`creativity`**, that helps an
operator discover useful possibilities when they cannot find a way forward.
The operator supplies a prompt describing the objective, available material,
facts, and constraints. The task explores combinations through a genetic
algorithm, using LLMs to construct the search material and evaluate candidates.

The capability is general. Finding a manuscript title and finding a business
initiative for 100 boxes of product that cannot be sold in China are examples,
not separate task types or hard-coded domains. The same motor must support
other objectives whose candidate possibilities can be represented and judged.

The result is a shortlist of meaningfully different proposals, with reasons,
assumptions, scores, and the reason the search ended. A score expresses an
evaluation against the objective; it is not a probability of real-world success.

The task is independently orderable through the existing task API and panel.
It uses existing execution, prompt routing, staffing, controls, and accounting
facilities. The task driver owns the evolutionary loop; LLMs own the semantic
work assigned to individual calls.

## Construct the search material from the problem

The initial contracted model call receives the actual prompt and relevant
source context. Its charge is: **understand this objective and create genes
that a genetic algorithm can combine into possible answers**.

It returns a compact representation containing:

- the objective and a decision-relevant summary of the source context;
- supplied facts and hard constraints, separated from assumptions and unknowns;
- the dimensions that can vary and a diverse set of variants for each;
- enough meaning and composition guidance to interpret a combination; and
- explicit evaluation criteria grounded in the operator's objective.

Genes are problem-dependent semantic components. They are not restricted to
words, two-word fragments, titles, business channels, or a fixed domain
catalogue. The LLM discovers useful dimensions from the charge. Their common
machine representation must remain simple enough for code to combine them.

Facts and constraints are not freely mutable genes. In the business example,
having 100 boxes and being unable to sell them in China remain conditions of
the search. A proposal may vary the allocation or use of those boxes; it cannot
invent more stock or remove the destination restriction. A material-specific
prompt cannot replace the operator's objective with its own preferred metric.

The compact problem description and criteria are task data carried into later
calls. Evolution changes possible answers without silently rewriting the
problem or repeatedly summarizing away its constraints.

## Evolution and evaluation

Code builds populations, selects parents, crosses their components, applies
ordinary mutation, and decides which candidates survive. The core crossover
does not require an LLM to invent each child. A candidate records a combination
whose meaning can be interpreted against the common problem context.

An evaluation call receives the objective, context summary, constraints,
criteria, and one or more candidates. It interprets each combination faithfully
as a proposal and returns constraint validity, an explanation, relevant
assumptions, and a numeric score in **`0..1`**. It cannot quietly replace the
selected components with a different proposal to make the combination work.
Constraint violations exclude a candidate from selection; a high score cannot
compensate for invalidity. Unsupported feasibility or demand remains an
assumption rather than an invented fact.

Evaluation should support bounded batches and concurrent calls so throughput
does not require one serial model invocation per candidate. One evaluator is a
valid configuration. If several models participate, the design must state how
their assessments contribute to selection and keep scores comparable enough
for progress detection. Historical scores and parent prestige must not become
arguments supplied to the evaluator in favor of a candidate.

Selection preserves strong candidates while leaving room for diversity and
new material. Ordinary mutation remains possible during productive generations;
it does not wait for stagnation. The result should not collapse into many
cosmetic variations of one winner.

## Progress, stagnation, and renewed exploration

**While the search is progressing, continue within the current repertoire.
When it stagnates, ask an LLM to expand that repertoire.**

Progress is a meaningful improvement in the best valid candidate against a
reference, using a configurable minimum improvement and patience window.
Small cumulative improvements count. A single poor generation does not trigger
an intervention, and a lower population average after introducing diversity
does not establish stagnation.

After the configured window without sufficient improvement, a dedicated call
receives the original objective, the search material, promising candidates,
and a compact account of what has already been explored. It proposes new
variants that can open different possibilities. The task incorporates them
without discarding the best candidates and begins a new observation window.
This is semantic expansion in addition to ordinary algorithmic mutation.

At minimum, expansion can add variants within existing dimensions. Whether
changing the dimensions themselves is needed, and how that would preserve
existing candidates, is a design question; a general schema-evolution system
is not a prerequisite for the first useful version.

The order exposes population and generation limits, selection/diversity and
mutation controls, the minimum improvement, patience, and a maximum number of
expansion interventions without recovered progress. A configured evaluation
target may permit early completion, but a raw score crossing the target is not
by itself proof that the objective has been solved. The design must define
the target's confirmation rule if this stop mode is offered.

Progress never bypasses the configured work budget or generation cap. On
budget exhaustion or persistent stagnation, the task returns the best valid
proposals found and the actual stop reason. If none is valid, it reports that
outcome plainly. Changing evaluator configuration alone must not count as
creative progress; the comparison rule should remain lightweight and explicit.

The numbers discussed so far, such as 24 candidates, three generations of
patience, or a `0.02` improvement, are experimental examples, not fixed defaults
or acceptance thresholds.

## Prompts by job and material

Use Prompt Router as the prompt authority for the three semantic jobs:
**create genes**, **evaluate candidates**, and **expand genes after stagnation**.
Exact canonical job and kind identifiers belong to the design.

Each job has a complete generic prompt and a common result contract. Existing
`material_layers[job][material]` can refine how that job approaches literature,
business, or another owner-defined theme. For example, gene creation may look
for images, rhythm, and tensions in literature, or resources, recipients,
agreements, and alternative uses in a business problem.

Material guides the content of genes and judgments; it does not create a
different evolutionary engine or an incompatible gene format. An absent
specialization uses the generic base. The material comes from the owning
order/context and is shared by these jobs, respecting the project's material
authority. Automatic domain classification is not required.

Register the new jobs and enforce their structural result contracts in code.
Stored prose alone does not create validation. Subsequent refinement by
material should be prompt-document work through the existing router. Preserve
its live-reading behavior; this task does not introduce prompt versions,
snapshots, or a second prompt-assembly path.

## Staffing independently for each job

The operator must be able to configure **model families and the model/effort
selection independently for gene creation, candidate evaluation, and semantic
expansion**. One task-wide choice such as `medium` is not enough as the only
control surface. A strong initial analysis, inexpensive repeated evaluation,
and stronger expansion after stagnation must be expressible in one task.

Reuse Staffing Router and its configured family ladders and tuning. In this
system, `low`, `medium`, and `high` are **rigor levels** selecting model and
effort settings; they are not concrete models, family names, or necessarily
the model's reasoning effort. Selecting a rigor must resolve to the model and
effort configured for that job and family.

The operator-facing configuration must support a default plus independent
choices per job, including using different `low`/`medium`/`high` levels for
different jobs. Family assignment and model/effort tuning remain configurable
through staffing. The same family may perform all jobs, or different families
may be assigned; a multi-family ensemble is not mandatory. Evaluation
parallelism and batch size are separate choices from family and rigor.

For illustration only, an operator could choose gene creation at `high`,
evaluation at `low`, and expansion at `medium`, with independent family
assignments. No provider, model name, or effort value is hard-coded by this
goal. Optional changes between levels during execution must follow explicit
operator configuration, not an unbounded agent decision.

The current implementation already assigns families and tunes model/effort
per role, but rigor belongs to the staffing session and is not a per-call
argument. The design must choose the smallest coherent integration that
expresses the required per-job choices. A dedicated creativity staffing
configuration, suitable existing role bindings, or a scoped extension of
resolution should be evaluated on that basis. It must not implement a private
model router or temporarily change a shared session's rigor around concurrent
calls. A job's override must not change unrelated work under the same owner.

Actual family, model, effort, usage, and cost remain visible through existing
per-call evidence and accounting. If evaluator selection changes, the search
must apply the explicit comparison rule rather than treating a more generous
judge as a better candidate.

## Integration and evidence of completion

Reuse the public task lifecycle and presentation. The operator can inspect
the current job and generation, progress/stagnation, expansion interventions,
best candidates, resolved staffing, and aggregate usage and cost. Physical
calls are inspectable work within the task; creating one durable child task
per candidate is not required. Preserve existing task controls and charge
accounting without building a parallel scheduler or recovery system.

Completion should demonstrate:

- one generic task working on materially different objectives, including a
  language-oriented example and a constrained business example;
- genes derived from each problem, valid combinations, ordinary mutation,
  diversity, and faithful scored interpretations;
- productive generations continuing, cumulative improvement being recognized,
  stagnation triggering expansion, and limits returning an honest result;
- different family and rigor choices per job resolving through staffing,
  including bounded concurrent evaluation without cross-job interference; and
- generic and material-specific prompts sharing the same machine contracts.

A small practical comparison against direct LLM ideation under a similar
budget should inform the initial choices. Do not claim that evolution improves
creative quality solely because its own judge awarded higher scores.

This goal delivers an exploration capability and proposals for the operator
to assess. Acting on a business proposal, publishing a literary result, or
executing the chosen initiative requires its own instruction.
